title: Place keys on a consistent-hash ring
statement:
Step 2 · Capacity and placement

Consistent hashing maps a key to its clockwise successor on a ring. The numeric positions here are already hashed. A real system also needs stable hashing, virtual nodes, replication, and migration planning.

Build it

For each key position return the first node position ≥ key, wrapping to the smallest node when necessary. Node positions are distinct, nonempty, and in [0,99]; keys are also in that range.

Contract: Implement route using Python's standard library. Inputs satisfy the constraints stated here. Do not mutate the inputs. Use the provided helpers where present; they represent earlier steps.

Examples

Input: nodes = [10, 40, 90], keys = [0, 10, 11, 90, 99]
Expected: [10, 10, 40, 90, 10]
Input: nodes = [50], keys = [1, 99]
Expected: [50, 50]
Hint

Sort the nodes, use a lower-bound search, then wrap the resulting index.

Review your understanding

Add a node at position 30 to [10,40,90]. Which key interval moves, and why are virtual nodes useful?

Explain your reasoning in Notes before opening the worked solution. Passing the local checks completes this exercise; it does not certify production readiness or evaluate your design explanation.
